questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish access reviews from RBAC, least privilege, and segregation of duties?
options: Access reviews replace the need for RBAC entirely
Those three controls are preventive; access reviews are detective — they catch what slipped through anyway
Access reviews only apply to privileged accounts, never regular users
There is no meaningful difference between them
questions.explain: RBAC, least privilege, and SoD try to prevent a bad grant from happening; access reviews are the recurring check that finds whatever still got through despite those preventive controls.

questions.q: What is 'attestation' in the context of an access review?
options: An automatic report IT generates with no human review
A password reset performed on a quarterly schedule
A legal document signed only once, at hire, that never needs updating
A data owner's formal sign-off, person by person, that an access grant is still needed
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that only the business owner can judge whether access is still needed, which is why attestation by the data owner — not just IT running a report — is the defining feature of a real review.

questions.q: Besides a scheduled calendar cadence, which of these is given as an event that should trigger an unscheduled access review?
options: A role change, such as the 'Mover' event from the Joiner-Mover-Leaver lifecycle
An employee taking a scheduled vacation
A routine software update with no security implications
A minor change to a company's logo
questions.explain: The lesson lists role changes, new audit findings, security incidents, and reorganizations/system integrations as unscheduled triggers for a review.

questions.q: What does 'remediation' mean in this lesson's access review process?
options: A technical term for encrypting a database column
The actual correction — usually removal — of access flagged as no longer needed, tracked with an owner and a deadline
The process of granting new access to a requester
A synonym for the review itself, with no distinct meaning
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates finding a problem from fixing it: remediation is the tracked, accountable act of closing out flagged access, not just identifying it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is a review run entirely by IT, with no data-owner attestation, insufficient?
options: Data owners are required by law to run every review personally
IT is legally barred from running any access reports
IT can usually detect technical anomalies but can't judge whether access is still needed from a business standpoint
IT-run reviews always produce inaccurate permission lists
questions.explain: The lesson notes that IT can generate a list of who has access quickly, but only the business owner can judge whether that access is still justified — which is the gap attestation closes.
